q: how many hearts does an octopus have
why does an octopus have three hearts
how many brains does an octopus have
how many arms does an octopus have
a: The octopus is a soft-bodied, eight-limbed mollusk of the order Octopoda, famous for its intelligence, camouflage, and unusual anatomy. An octopus has three hearts: two branchial hearts that pump blood through the gills, and one systemic heart that circulates blood to the rest of the body — the two branchial hearts stop beating when the octopus swims, which is why they prefer to crawl. It also has nine brains: one central brain plus a mini-brain in each arm, allowing each arm to act somewhat independently. Octopuses are masters of camouflage, changing color, texture, and even shape in under a second using chromatophore cells in their skin, and they can regrow lost arms. They are solitary hunters that live in reefs and the deep sea worldwide, and their intelligence — tool use, problem-solving, and escape artistry — is considered among the highest of any invertebrate.
